chunks.t: The Global Service Team (GST) helps clubs identify resources and use best practices to improve their projects and, by extension, their impact. Quality service projects increase member satisfaction and help attract new members who are looking to serve. The GST champions the service programs, resources and grants of Lions Clubs International and Lions Clubs International Foundation (LCIF), empowering Lions and Leos around the world to maximize their service impact. Lions Clubs International Global Causes Over the last 100 years, the kindness of Lions and Leos has multiplied across borders, oceans, and continents. With over 1.4 million members, we now have an opportunity to truly change our world. That’s why we’re uniting our global service around five areas of need.

These Global Causes present significant challenges to humanity, and we believe it’s our turn to meet them. The Service Journey, Service Toolkit and Service Launchpad The Service Journey is an approach to living and serving well. To making a real difference people can see and feel. It encompasses four simple phases: Learn, Discover, Act, and Celebrate. We love these words because they transcend organizational formulas. They have no borders. They are the essence of Lions and Leos. Service Programs, Project Planners and Project Ideas Lions Clubs International has a number of service project opportunities. Join Lions around the world in serving our global causes. Learn more about Lions Clubs International service programs and get resources to help plan service projects.

Advocacy Lions listen to the needs of their communities and are voices to create change. Advocacy is a new way you can serve to further the mission of Lions Clubs International, Lions Clubs International Foundation, and the causes you care about. You can participate in advocacy by using your voice—through community awareness and education, legislation and public policy, events and partnerships. As community leaders, Lions and Leos can speak for those who need to be heard in front of those who need to hear them. Service at the Lions Clubs International Convention Convention service projects allow Lions and Leos attending convention to experience first-hand, how host city Lions serve those in need. Projects take place at the convention center and at various locations throughout the host city.

Lions-Elevance Health Volunteer Days Lions International has partnered with the Elevance Health Foundation since 2015 to provide volunteer engagement opportunities for Elevance Health employees within their local communities. Clubs in specified cities across the US submit project proposals each spring in order to receive up to US$2,500 in grant funding for the implementation and execution of a service project that engages Elevance Health employees, friends and family members. Service Reporting When we share our service stories and report our service, we inform, inspire and build our humanitarian legacy. On our service reporting webpage, you can find more reporting benefits, information on how to report service and ways to measure your club’s impact.

Service Awards The Kindness Matters Service Award is given annually to a handful of Lions and Leo clubs for performing an outstanding service project in one of our global cause areas. Nominated at the club level, the Kindness Matters Service Award is a challenge for Lions and Leos to develop exceptionally innovative and creative service projects with the aim of leaving a positive impact in their communities. Lions Clubs International Foundation Grants There are a wide variety of grants available to help Lions serve their local communities and the world. We encourage you to explore the different grant types to find out if there’s a grant that’s right for your club, district or multiple district now or in the future. So whether you’re recruiting new members, promoting a project or a fundraiser, or even just sharing your incredible service stories, marketing can help you shine a light on your club and your service. Find your fit Club marketing is so important to what we do, and there are great opportunities to get involved. Getting started with supporting Leos Lead the next generation Leo Club Advisors Leo club advisors As a Leo club advisor, your enthusiasm about working with young people and guiding Leos in club management and service is key to ensuring their success. In addition, you play an important role in kickstarting the collaboration between Leos and your Lions club, creating an environment for learning and connecting Leos with other community leaders. Understanding your role Some responsibilities of your role can vary depending on your Leos’ ages — Omega Leos may require different support than Alpha Leos, like when executing service projects or developing leadership skills. But regardless of which club you’re sponsoring, there are tasks that you’ll need to support and training to help you do it.

Talk to Lion leaders supporting Leos Be sure to maintain open communication with the district and multiple district Leo chairpersons, as well as Leo leaders at those levels, to ensure full support for your Leo club. Report your Leos Take time to report any new Leo members, clubs and service projects in the Lion Portal to help track the health of the club and to see the service impact Leos have made. Learn more about the importance of reporting in the Reporting Matters Guide. Order supplies Explore Leo-branded items in the Lions Shop to help recognize your Leos and show your Leo pride. You can also order recruitment materials and the Leo Club Program Handbook using the Leo Club Publications Order Form.

Attend a Leo forum Leo forums can help you understand the Leo Club Program and network with other Lions and Leos so you can find new ideas for service, build connections and more. You can also find more information about what your role entails in the Leo Club Program Handbook. Supporting Leos’ next service steps As Leos consider serving as a Lion or approach the end of their time in the Leo Club Program, it’s important to talk with them about continuing their service journey and to let them know they have options. Alpha Leos may find Omega Leos to be a natural next step. In addition to Omega Leos, encouraging Leos to become Lions is an excellent way to help Leos to continue to grow their impact.

If Alpha or Omega Leos do not transfer their membership before aging out of the Leo Club Program, their respective records will be automatically closed, or end-dated, by Lions International annually on June 30 according to Board Policy Chapter XXII, Article V., C. Be sure to let your Leos know that continuing their service journey will help keep their service record intact. Other ways to help your Leos In addition to the logistical steps required in your role, there are other steps you can take to help your Leos and your Leo club grow. Set your club up for success Learn how you and your fellow Lions club officers can help your Leo club start strong with tips on member recruitment, promoting the club and much more.

The training includes six modules that cover important tips, tools and resources that can help you find success in supporting your Leos. Module 1: Leo Club Program overview Learn about the history, purpose and structure of the Leo Club Program.

Power Point Module 2: The role of the Leo club advisor Get a better understanding of the responsibilities of your role as well as strategies for serving as effective advisors and promoting positive youth development. Power Point Module 4: Leo Club Program resources from Lions International Learn about resources and tools available from Lions International to support Leo club advisors. , recognized annually on October 15, gives Lions an opportunity to increase awareness of the white cane and associated pedestrian and traffic safety laws. Why we celebrate Throughout the world, the long white cane is used by people with visual impairment or blindness as a tool for safe and reliable navigation. The white cane is a symbol of the user’s skills and talents, mobility and independence. Many states, provinces, or local areas offer classes for visually impaired individuals to learn how to effectively use a white cane. The white cane acts as a safety measure, alerting motorists and universally acknowledging the user as visually impaired. Sometimes the white cane has a red band or strip for the purpose of contrast.

Today, white cane laws and regulations exist in multiple countries around the world, providing visually impaired individuals a legal status in traffic. White cane history and Lions service 1921James Biggs, a photographer from Bristol, England, became blind following an accident. Because he was feeling uncomfortable with the amount of traffic around his home, he painted his walking stick white to be more easily visible.1930Lion George A. Bonham, President of the Peoria Lions Club in Illinois, United States, introduced the idea of using a white cane with a red band as a means of assisting the blind in independent mobility after noticing a visually impaired individual’s guide stick was black and not very noticeable.

The club distributed white canes, and the Peoria City Council adopted an ordinance giving users the right-of-way to cross the street.1931Guilly d’Herbemont launched a national “white stick movement” in France, symbolically giving the first two white canes to visually impaired people in the presence of French ministers. Overwhelming universal acceptance of the white cane quickly gave users a unique method of identifying their special need for travel consideration among other pedestrians and motorists.

1964The United States Congress approved a resolution authorizing the President of the United States to annually issue a proclamation designating October 15 as “National White Cane Safety Day.” In 1969, the International Federation of the Blind (now the World Blind Union), adopted the date as “International White Cane Safety Day.” Suggested activities for Lions Mobilize your club to partner with local schools, community groups and organizations for the visually impaired to plan your International White Cane Day activity. Invite a representative from a school or organization for the visually impaired to speak about the white cane and white cane regulations in your community. Connect with government officials to create an International White Cane Day proclamation for your event.

Advocate by working with community leaders to improve accessibility and safety. Visit the Advocacy at Lions International webpage to get started. Work with organizations or agencies for the visually impaired to provide white canes to those in need in your community. The National Federation of the Blind offers free white canes to people with blindness in the United States. Distribute flyers and share safety messages through local media educating drivers and pedestrians on what a white cane signifies and how to respond safely. Raise awareness of the white cane through a social media campaign: post stories, opportunities to advocate, and educational material and use the #International White Cane Day hashtag. Resources Learn about the United Nations Development Programme’s work to promote International White Cane Day.

Discover how UNICEF promotes inclusion and advocates for access. Explore the Lions International Vision webpage which features information on vision programs, LCIF grant opportunities, and how to make a donation to empower the service of Lions around the world. Publicize your service by utilizing marketing toolkits and resources on the Lions International Club Marketing webpage. Report your vision service Be sure to report your service in the Lion Portal to showcase your club’s impact and inspire others. Report your service

Provide leadership development opportunities in your area by hosting a Lions Leadership Institute. Grants are available to support eligible multiple districts, single districts, and undistricted regions and zones in delivering select institute programs. Funds available Multiple districtsUS$4500Single districtsUS$1800UndistrictedUS$750Applications awarded100% Choose the best institute for your area Designed for Lions and Leos who are beginning their leadership journey, ELLI builds foundational skills and confidence for club-level roles. It is best suited for areas looking to develop emerging leaders and prepare them for future responsibilities within the club and beyond. Part of the Lions Leadership Development pathway. Multiple districts, single districts, and undistricted regions and zones are eligible to apply.

ELLI is a three-day institute with a standard curriculum that ensures a consistent training experience worldwide. Participants gain practical leadership skills to support effective teamwork, communication and club success. The ELLI curriculum is provided upon approval of the grant application. ELLIDesigned for Lions with some leadership experience, RLLI strengthens and expands leadership skills for increased effectiveness at the club and district levels. It is best suited for areas looking to prepare leaders for more advanced roles. Part of the Lions Leadership Development pathway. Multiple districts, single districts, and undistricted regions and zones are eligible to apply. Grant-funded RLLIs must follow a three-day format.

Each institute includes four required core sessions, along with elective sessions selected by organizers to meet local needs. The RLLI curriculum is provided upon approval of the grant application. RLLIDesigned for Lions who will serve as trainers, FDI develops facilitation skills to deliver effective Lions learning programs. It is best suited for areas looking to build or strengthen a qualified faculty base. Part of the Lions Train-the-Trainer pathway. Only multiple districts and single districts are eligible to apply for a local FDI. The institute includes a structured curriculum focused on foundational facilitation skills. Participants develop the skills needed to effectively deliver and support Lions training programs. The FDI curriculum is provided upon approval of the grant application.

Anniversaries remind us of our milestones and give us the opportunity to celebrate, commemorate and reflect. Lions International recognizes our members’ anniversaries by presenting them with Chevron Awards. What are Chevron Awards? Chevron Awards are given to Lions to commemorate their years of service and encourage them to continue making a difference in their local communities and worldwide. There are two types — Charter Monarch Chevron Awards and Monarch Chevron Awards — that Lions may receive. Once a Lion has met all the necessary requirements, the award is automatically shipped to the current year’s district governor between July and September and presented to the winning Lion at a district convention or other celebration.

Eligibility and criteria To receive a Charter Monarch Chevron Award or a Monarch Chevron Award, the following eligibility requirements and criteria must be met: Charter Monarch Chevron Award This award is given only to club chartering Lions who have served for 10 years, continuing every five years until their 95th year of service. Monarch Chevron Award This award is given to any Lion who has served for 10 years, continuing every five years until their 95th year of service. Contact and additional resources If you have questions or need a replacement award, contact us at . To learn more about other membership awards or how to start a new club, the following webpages will give you all the information you need. Membership Awards Start a New Club

Getting started with supporting Leos Why sponsor a Leo club Starting a Leo club Starting a Leo club By sponsoring a Leo club, you have the opportunity to empower young leaders and guide the next generation of service. Leo club types and tracks Within the Leo Club Program, there are different options for the type of club and ages of Leos you can sponsor. Explore the options to see which track and club type works best for the young people in your community. Club types As a club sponsor, you can choose to start one of two types of clubs — a community-based club designed for any eligible young person, or a school-based Leo club that takes place in a school setting with additional leadership from school staff. Tracks There are two tracks in the Leo Club Program based on age. Alpha Leos are for ages 12–18, and Omega Leos are for ages 18-30.

The type of service — as well as overall leadership style — will vary based on the ages of your Leos, so keep that in mind as you plan your sponsorship. Steps to starting a club Once you’ve identified your Leo club advisor and determined the type of Leo club you’re starting, follow the steps outlined below to help ensure your new club has a successful start — and is ready to make an impact in your community. You can find more in-depth information on how to choose the right Leo club advisor, as well as the steps below, in the Leo Club Starter Guide. As you begin the steps to start your new Leo club, make sure to review the related fees, including a one-time organization fee starting at US$100 and an annual Leo club sponsor levy thereafter of US$100 both of which may increase depending on the size of your club.

Explore the Leo Club Program Fees resource to learn more. Step 1: Identify members and advertise the club Take note of potential Leos from friends, relatives, educational institutions, houses of worship or other youth-centered organizations and market your new club to those audiences. Be sure to use tools and resources from the Marketing Matters webpage to make your club marketing stand out!Step 2: Invite prospects to an informational meeting Once you’ve identified prospective members, invite them to a meeting where you’ll explain what your Leo club is all about, answer any questions and get them excited about joining. Be sure to have an Alpha Application for Leo Club Membership or an Omega Application for Leo Club Membership to give to your prospective members.

Step 3: Host a formation meeting Once you have your Leo members in place, host a formation meeting where Leos will accept the Leo Club Constitution and Bylaws, elect Leo club officers and determine club meeting times and location. Step 4: Complete required logistics Fill out the Leo Club Organization Report and collect the proper signatures needed, then submit the form to . The new Leo club application can also be submitted in the Lion Portal at lionportal.org. Once received, the certification process can take four to six weeks to finalize. Step 5: Plan an installment ceremony After your Leo Club Organization Report is approved, plan a ceremony to present the Certificate of Organization and formally install your Leo club officers using the Leo Club Officer Installation and New Member Initiation Guide.

Grow your club Once your Leo club is established, it’s important to keep recruiting so your club can build a strong foundation that will keep the club up and running for years to come. Use the Leo Recruitment Brochure and the Leo Recruitment Poster to give to prospective members so they can learn more about the Leo Club Program and your club. Support your club Learn more about the ways you can further support your Leo club, from roles for your Lions to encouraging Leo club officer training and inspiring Leos to become Lions members as they near the end of the Leo Club Program.

chunks.h: Leo and Leo-Lion Awards and Recognition
chunks.t: Lions International offers an array of awards to recognize Leos and Lions who are active in the Leo Club Program, as well as Leo-Lions. There are more than 20 award programs to acknowledge their accomplishments. Please note that only Leo and Lion officers reported to Lions International are eligible to receive awards and certificates. Processing time: Please allow 2-4 weeks after receipt of required forms. Leo Awards Individual Leos, Leo club advisors and Leo clubs as well as their sponsoring clubs have the opportunity to earn a variety of prestigious awards. Check out all the available awards and their qualifications.

chunks.h: Leo and Leo-Lion Awards and Recognition
chunks.t: Individual Leo and Leo Advisor Awards Leos of the Year Award: A multiple district council of governors or single district (that is not part of a multiple district) may nominate one high-achieving Leo each year for this medallion and certificate award. Applications must be submitted by March 1. Congratulations to all the current award recipients!Leo Club President Achievement Award: A Leo club president who meets specific requirements during their year in office may be awarded this certificate by the Leo club advisor with the approval of the sponsoring Lions club president. Award criteria categories include leadership development, membership extension, administration and Leo club activities. Certificate will be emailed to Leo club advisors in May.

chunks.h: Leo and Leo-Lion Awards and Recognition
chunks.t: Leo October Membership Growth Award: Leo club advisors may present this award to any Leo who is reported in the Lion Portal as a sponsor for at least three new members who join during the month of October. Leo club advisors whose Leos meet the above criteria by November 15 will be sent the award automatically; no application is necessary. Leo Award of Honor: Leos may nominate a fellow Leo member for this award to recognize their outstanding accomplishments during the year. The lapel medal can be purchased from the Lions Shop. Leo Club Advisor Outstanding Service Award: The Leo club president may present this award to Leo club advisors who meet specific requirements and demonstrate outstanding service in guiding and developing their Leo clubs. Nomination forms are accepted April-June each year.

chunks.h: Leo and Leo-Lion Awards and Recognition
chunks.t: Leo Club Advisor Five-Year Service Award: Sponsoring Lions club presidents may honor Leo club advisors who successfully complete five years of dedicated service with this award. Sponsoring Lions club presidents should complete and submit this application to obtain the five-year service pin and certificate. Leo Club Sponsorship Recognition Award: Sponsoring Lions club presidents and Leo club advisors receive these certificates upon official certification of a new Leo club. The sponsoring Lions club can request additional certificates by emailing  for anyone it wishes to thank for assisting in organizing the new Leo club. Leo Clubs and Sponsoring Lions Clubs Leo Club Pride Award: Leo clubs that have excelled in reporting their service, member and officer information will receive the Leo Club Pride Award.

chunks.h: Leo and Leo-Lion Awards and Recognition
chunks.t: Clubs who meet the following criteria based on reports in the Lion Portal by June 30 will be sent the award automatically; no application is necessary. Leo Club Excellence Award: All districts may endorse one Leo club to receive this prestigious award. Applications are due May 31. Winners will receive a banner patch and chevron in Leo colors. Congratulations to all the current award recipients!Serving Together Award: A banner patch featuring the Leo and Lions club logo is awarded to both the Leo club and the sponsoring Lions club for successful completion of joint projects and other types of activities supporting Leo and Lion collaboration. Award requirements are on the application. Award can be received once per Lion year. Ideas to successfully work together can be found on the Leo and Lion Positive Collaboration webpage.

chunks.h: Leo and Leo-Lion Awards and Recognition
chunks.t: Leo Club and Sponsoring Lions Club Anniversary Patches: Leo clubs who have achieved the fifth anniversary of their certification and their sponsoring Lions club can receive anniversary patches sent from the Leo Club Program staff. Patches are sent for anniversaries in multiples of five years thereafter. To receive the anniversary patch, please complete the following form. Leo Club Sponsorship Patch: A banner patch is issued to the sponsoring Lions club upon certification of a new Leo club. Leo District and Multiple Districts Leo District President Achievement Award: A Leo district president who meets specific requirements during their year in office may be awarded this certificate at the end of the Lion year by the district Leo chairperson with the approval of the district governor.

chunks.h: Leo and Leo-Lion Awards and Recognition
chunks.t: Award criteria categories include leadership development, club or membership extension, administration and district Leo activities. Certificate will be emailed to district Leo chairpersons in May. Leo Multiple District President Achievement Award: A Leo multiple district president who meets specific requirements during their year in office may be awarded this certificate at the end of the Lion year by the multiple district Leo chairperson with the approval of the council chairperson. Award criteria categories include leadership development, club or membership extension, administration and multiple district Leo activities. Certificate will be emailed to multiple district Leo chairpersons in May.

chunks.h: Leo and Leo-Lion Awards and Recognition
chunks.t: Leo Club Extension Award: Certificates are awarded to district Leo chairpersons and Leo district presidents who achieve a net gain of three new clubs in their district, and to multiple district Leo chairpersons and Leo multiple district presidents who achieve a net gain of five new clubs in their multiple district by June 30. Additional eligibility criteria includes that all new Leo clubs must report all members and their five club officers, and at least one service project must be reported in the Lion Portal during that fiscal year. No application is necessary. Leo-Lion Awards Leo-Lion awards are automatically processed after the end of each fiscal year — no need to apply!

chunks.h: Leo and Leo-Lion Awards and Recognition
chunks.t: Processing for these awards will occur after June 30 of each fiscal year so that data from the entire fiscal year can be used, and certificates will be sent in the following months. Leo-to-Lion Transition Awards Leo to Leo-Lion Membership Award: Special certificates are awarded to Leo club advisors, district Leo chairpersons and multiple district Leo chairpersons who have facilitated the transition of Leos to Leo-Lion members between July 1 through June 30. The following criteria applies for these awards: Leo club advisors: Guide five or more Leos from their Leo clubs to transition to Leo-Lion members. District Leo chairpersons: Facilitate Leo to Leo-Lion membership for 15 or more Leos from Leo clubs within their district.

chunks.h: Leo and Leo-Lion Awards and Recognition
chunks.t: Multiple district Leo chairpersons: Facilitate Leo to Leo-Lion membership for 30 or more Leos from any districts within their multiple district. Awards for Sponsoring Leo-Lion Clubs Leo-Lion Club Charter Award: Special certificates are awarded to sponsoring Lions clubs, district governors, district Leo chairpersons and multiple district Leo chairpersons who have facilitated the new charters of one or more Leo-Lion clubs. Completed charters must be approved by Lions Clubs International between July 1 through June 30 of the respective fiscal year. The following criteria applies for these awards: Lions clubs: Sponsor one or more newly chartered Leo-Lion clubs. District Leo chairpersons and district governors: Facilitate one or more new Leo-Lion club charters within their district.

chunks.h: Leo and Leo-Lion Awards and Recognition
chunks.t: Multiple district Leo chairpersons: Facilitate one or more new Leo-Lion club charters within any of their districts. Leo and Leo-Lion Awards Presidential Awards Initiatives Presidential awards are created annually and may include additional awards regarding Leos, Leo-Lions or the membership of young people. See this year’s presidential awards to find out more about whether awards are available regarding Leos and Leo-Lions. LCIF Awards Leos and Leo-Lions are eligible for a number of awards and recognition presented by the Lions Clubs International Foundation (LCIF). These include a certificate of appreciation, LCIF Chairperson’s certificate, Melvin Jones Fellowship, banner patch and club plaque award. Contact LCIF for more information.

chunks.h: Leo and Leo-Lion Awards and Recognition
chunks.t: Kindness Matters Service Award The Kindness Matters Service Award is a prestigious award that is given annually to a handful of Lions and Leo clubs for performing an outstanding service project in one of Lions International’s global cause areas. Nominated at the club level, the Kindness Matters Service Award is a challenge for Lions and Leos to develop exceptionally innovative and creative service projects with the aim of leaving a positive impact in their communities. Lions International Marketing Award Leo and Leo-Lion clubs have the chance to be recognized for great club marketing. Clubs must plan and execute a marketing campaign that meets the award criteria and only one Leo or Lion club per constitutional area will win. Check out the full award details and apply here.

chunks.h: Leo and Leo-Lion Awards and Recognition
chunks.t: If you have questions or need more information about any Leo or Leo-Lion awards, contact the Young Lions and Leos Department staff.

Reaching out to communities to save sight Eighty percent of all visual impairment can be prevented or cured. The first step to prevention is awareness. The second is early detection through vision screening. Around the world, Lions partner with medical professionals and community leaders to screen young children, primary school students, and adults to identify those at risk for vision loss. The venue for Lions’ vision screenings varies from schools, to workplaces, to community health fairs, and the screening methods depend upon the age group. But the results are always the same. Early identification leads to timely referral, professional treatment, and improved or restored sight. Vision Screening for Adults A vision screening event for adults that promotes eye health and raises community awareness of the causes of preventable vision loss.

Vision Screening for Children A vision screening event for children in local primary, middle, or secondary schools that identifies those who may have vision problems requiring comprehensive follow-up by eye care professionals.

Is your district or multiple district looking for a speaker for your district/multiple district wide event or convention? You can submit a request for an official Lions speaker here. Please read the considerations below, and then fill out the form. If you have any questions, please email us at . Considerations Each district (single, sub and multiple) shall be allowed one official speaker for its convention or similar districtwide function, per fiscal year, from within their constitutional area. The official speaking assignment must be for a districtwide function that represents the entire district, and an event in which all clubs within the district are invited to participate.

The host district (single, sub and multiple) will be responsible for all local expenses for the authorized speakers, including accommodations cost, meals and local transportation. If a district fails to meet this obligation, the district will not be eligible for a speaker for future events until the debt has been paid. This form must be completed by the District Governor, for district or sub district events, or Council Chairperson, for multiple district events, and must be submitted to the Travel Department at least sixty (60) days prior to the date of the function. The sixty (60) day requirement shall be waived only in the event of an emergency requiring a substitute speaker or in cases where the second or third vice president or a first year director is requested for an authorized meeting scheduled for July, August or September.

Speaker photos and biographies are available for download from our website. Acknowledgement of the receipt of the form will be sent out within 48 hours of receipt, to the District Governor or Council Chairperson. Complete Form

Lions and Johnson & Johnson Lions Clubs International Foundation (LCIF) and Johnson & Johnson co-founded Sight For Kids (SFK), the largest-known, school-based eye health program that mobilizes Lions and eye care professionals to provide comprehensive eye health services in low-income schools around the world. Responding to a need According to Johnson & Johnson, Myopia, often called nearsightedness, is commonly understood as the inability to see distant objects clearly without glasses or contact lenses. It is, in fact, much more than that. Myopia is a chronic progressive disease where continued eye growth not only worsens distance vision, it also increases future risk of sight-threatening complications. In 2002, LCIF and Johnson & Johnson offered a solution.

For over 20 years, Johnson & Johnson and LCIF have been on a mission to transform eye health for school-aged children worldwide through Sight For Kids. Together, we celebrate how this initiative is providing kids with the vision they need to succeed in their education and beyond. It’s for the kids More than 50 million children have been impacted through the Sight For Kids program since its inception. Explore impactful stories from our collaboration.
